title: Point-Query Optimized Index Overkill
pattern: A developer or DBA adds indexes to every single column in a relational database table to ensure that every potential search query is blazingly fast.
why_bad: Locally, individual SELECT queries are fast. Globally, it severely degrades write performance and bloats storage. Every time a row is inserted, updated, or deleted, *every single index* must also be updated. This turns a simple, sequential insert into a flurry of random write operations across multiple index structures, inflating write amplification and disk latency.
detection: Database schemas where the number of indexes is equal to or exceeds the number of columns, or where tables with high write-to-read ratios are heavily indexed.
counterexample: Valid for read-only static reference tables where writes occur only during nightly batch jobs. Mark `Context-dependent`.
source: Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 3, "SSTables and LSM-Trees: Indexing Overhead" (p. 77, 81) / Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, "Verify gains against real data" (p. 293).
